solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Same ship, different stress

indicators.note: made different, so the letters of the two words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The same vessel, but the tension aboard has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress laid on a word or point, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Servant in upset during dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: placed during the meal means the other piece goes inside it

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

indicators.note: upset as in turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the word backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A domestic gets upset while serving dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic servant doing lowly work.

clue.text: Audience with half-hour to spend

indicators.note: half of the word that follows means keeping only its first two letters

parts.note: to use something up is to spend it

explanation.surface: A theatre crowd with thirty minutes to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's house is its audience, as in a full house.

clue.text: Idler soon roused to continue regardless

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy person, quickly woken, carries on anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for persevering despite difficulty.

clue.text: Wrongly presume it's the highest

indicators.note: taken in the wrong way, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly assumes something is top.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means greatest in rank or degree.

clue.text: Not French, but Latin accepted

parts.note: pas is the French for not
sed is the Latin for but

explanation.surface: A language lesson: a word isn't French, but it is Latin and so gets through.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion that is passed has been accepted or approved.

clue.text: Helen's favourite city

definitions.meaning: the Trojan prince who carried off Helen of Troy

explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan who eloped with Helen shares his name with the French capital.

clue.text: It might be last straw for loyal supporters

indicators.note: the letters might be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Even faithful fans can reach a breaking point.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwarts are steadfast, dependable supporters.

clue.text: Put a full stop at the end of a sentence?

definitions.text: Put a full stop at the end of a sentence?

parts.words: Put a full stop at the end of a sentence?
parts.note: sounds like punctuation, but describes a death sentence ending in a life being stopped

explanation.definitionFit: A condemned prisoner put to death has had the court's sentence carried out.

clue.text: Garden flower periodical

definitions.meaning: a plant that lives for one season
a yearbook or publication issued once a year

explanation.definitionFit: An annual is both a one-season garden plant and a book published yearly.

clue.text: Shared a good round of golf?

definitions.meaning: took part in or had a portion of
read playfully as having taken par, the standard score for a course

explanation.definitionFit: To have partaken is to have shared in something; split, it reads as par having been taken.

clue.text: You may lose a whole day going over it

definitions.text: You may lose a whole day going over it

parts.words: You may lose a whole day going over it
parts.note: sounds like a tedious review, but describes crossing the line in the Pacific where the calendar date changes

explanation.definitionFit: The international date line is where travellers skip or repeat a calendar day.

clue.text: Satisfactorily completed and mended

definitions.meaning: an idiom for a deal or task wrapped up and settled
literally stitched back together with needle and thread

explanation.definitionFit: Sewn up is an idiom for settled and also literally means stitched closed.

clue.text: Not the complete games player?

parts.note: seems to criticise a partial athlete, but names a rugby back position whose title suggests a fraction of a whole

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an incomplete sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the backs between the halfbacks and the full-back are called by this fractional name, so 'not the complete' player is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-quarter is a rugby back, and the name literally means less than whole.

clue.text: Happen to finish in the first three

definitions.text: to finish in the first three
definitions.meaning: in racing, finishing in a placing position

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occur, and in racing to be placed among the leaders.

clue.text: A bilingual graduate, put off but not disconcerted

parts.note: the word a given in two languages: un in French, then a in English
BA is a Bachelor of Arts
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: A graduate fluent in two tongues stays calm after being rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bilingual' means 'a' in two languages: French UN plus English A.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed means unembarrassed, not put out.

clue.text: Versatile languages master?

parts.note: describes a person who has command of many tongues

explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot is someone who speaks many languages.

clue.text: Wage-earners, for example, on form

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual wage-earners are a classic example of the social group so named.

clue.text: It goes on incessantly, even when idle

definitions.text: It goes on incessantly, even when idle

parts.words: It goes on incessantly, even when idle
parts.note: sounds like an engine running, but is idle talk that never stops

explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is continual trivial talk, often called idle.

clue.text: Bill has little money, resulting in stress

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Money worries from a bill and almost nothing in the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the stress placed on a syllable.

clue.text: It limits one's outlook

parts.note: seems to describe narrow-mindedness, but is literally a condition restricting how far one can see

explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness literally limits vision, and figuratively a narrow outlook.

clue.text: Where ladies wear new hats and new coats

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fashion note on hats and coats bought for an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is an English racecourse whose Ladies' Day is famous for extravagant hats.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse is famed for its Ladies' Day hat parade.

clue.text: In an emergency with a bugging device, move slowly

parts.note: a tap is a device for listening in on a phone line
to inch is to creep forward bit by bit

explanation.surface: In a crisis, with a listening device fitted, creep along carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, as one would act in an emergency.

clue.text: Northern block house

parts.note: sounds like a terraced home in the north of England, but is a dwelling made of blocks of snow in the Arctic

explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is built of blocks of packed snow in the far north.

clue.text: Neat gash with no dirt in it

parts.note: something with no dirt is clean
a gash is a cut

explanation.surface: A tidy wound kept free of infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut means neat and sharply defined, or tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Bluff king and his successor brought to a temporary stop

parts.note: Bluff King Hal is the nickname of Henry VIII
Henry VIII was succeeded by Edward VI, and Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A hearty monarch and his heir bring proceedings to a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff King Hal' is a traditional English nickname for Henry VIII; his son and successor was Edward VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Halted means stopped, often only for a while.

clue.text: Confirm a man refusing strong drink is French

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who abstains from alcohol
est is the French for is

explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to vouch for or bear witness, so to confirm.

clue.text: Old soldiers scared to set off

indicators.note: set off as in set going in another direction, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Veterans too frightened to march out.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of former times, named for their scarlet tunics.
